newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour party denies Argentine Falklands deal.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour party denies Argentine Falklands deal.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party denied on Tuesday that it would hand the disputed Falkland Islands back to Argentina if it wins the general election.
"There is not a shred of truth in the suggestion that there might be any change of policy towards the Falklands were Labour to be elected on May 1," the party said in a statement.
"If the Argentinians are anticipating any change in UK approach they are mistaken and ignoring the clear message given to both islanders and the Argentine government over recent years," it added.

Labour issued the statement after Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez reportedly told Jane's Defence Weekly that he and Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella had met several Labour Party officials, including leader Tony Blair.
"I believe that, after May 1, a new phase of review of the Malvinas (Falklands) with a new administration will start," he is quoted as saying.
Labour also denied that Blair, highly tipped to win the May 1 election, had meetings or discussions with Di Tella.
Britain and Argentina fought a 10-week war over the islands in 1982. Although Argentina lost, it maintains its claims to the sparsely populated archipelago which it calls the Malvinas.

The two countries have restored diplomatic relations and in 1995 signed a deal to explore for oil in the waters around the Falklands, but fishing rights and sovereignty of the islands have been a stumbling block in closer ties.
